kurz: How funds, shares and loans provide access to property without an entry in the land register, and how much they differ in time limits, pricing and default risk.

bloecke.md: There are three ways to invest in property without being entered in the land register yourself: through a fund that buys buildings, through a public limited company that owns buildings and through a loan to a project developer who constructs buildings. All they have in common is that the incidental purchase costs of a direct investment do not apply on entry. When buying a flat, these amount to around 4.5% to just under 12%, depending on the federal state and whether an estate agent is involved, and are lost immediately. Otherwise, the three routes differ more than the common umbrella term would suggest. The fund is a segregated pool of assets (Sondervermögen) with statutory time limits, the share is subject to the usual price fluctuations, and the loan is unsecured credit.

## Open-ended real estate funds

An **open-ended real estate fund** is a segregated pool of assets that holds commercial and residential properties and continuously issues new units. The unit price is determined on every stock exchange trading day. This often leads to a misunderstanding, because a price calculated daily means neither that the units can be sold daily nor that the price was formed in the market.

Since the German Investment Code (Kapitalanlagegesetzbuch, KAGB) of 2013, the time limits have been laid down by law. A **minimum holding period** of 24 months applies to units acquired. Redemption must be declared irrevocably with a **notice period** of twelve months. Payment is made at the unit price applicable on the redemption date, and nobody knows this price on the day notice is given. If the fund's liquid assets are then insufficient, it may suspend redemptions, for up to 36 months in the case of retail funds. The level of these assets varies widely. The funds' liquidity ratio ranges from 5% to 49% of fund assets.

bloecke.titel: What happens after notice is given
bloecke.unter: During the twelve-month notice period, the fund must raise the necessary liquidity, and during this time the investor does not know the payout price.

knoten.notiz: at the earliest after a 24-month holding period

bloecke.md:
The reason for these rules is maturity transformation. An office building cannot be sold in three days, whereas a fund unit can. The product worked as long as not many investors returned units at the same time. The KAGB time limits are the legislature's response to such a crisis.

In addition, there is the pricing. The unit value is based on appraisals and not on stock exchange prices. External valuers estimate the market value of each property at fixed intervals, and between two valuation dates the value remains unchanged. As a result, performance is as smooth as that of an interest-bearing savings balance and is therefore regularly mistaken for low risk. The low volatility is a **valuation artefact**; it is caused by the valuation method and is not a characteristic of the properties. The risk remains, because changes in market conditions are only reflected in the unit value with the next appraisal, but then all at once.

Here, performance without visible swings is a consequence of the valuation method and not a sign of stable property prices. Investors who use such funds as a substitute for an instant-access savings account or as a “low-volatility building block” take on two characteristics they do not want. Their money is tied up for at least twelve months, and write-downs appear in jumps instead of gradually.

Units can also be sold immediately and without a notice period on the stock exchange, but this second way out is rarely better. A real market price applies there, and it is well below the official unit value, especially when many investors want to sell at the same time.

bloecke.unter: The figures from 2008 to 2013 are documented; the development of valuations since the turn in the interest rate cycle is deliberately described without percentages.

ereignisse.text: After the Lehman collapse, institutional investors in particular return units on a large scale. Several funds suspend redemptions because properties cannot be sold within a few weeks.

17 funds have to dispose of properties under pressure to sell. The largest single write-down is recorded by Degi Global Business at minus 21.6%. In the end, investors' losses add up to around €8.3 billion.
24-month minimum holding period and 12-month notice period; redemptions can still be suspended for up to 36 months.

A partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) of 60% applies to real estate funds, or 80% for funds with a foreign focus. The reform replaces the former transparency principle, under which investors paid tax on the income as if they held the properties themselves.

ereignisse.titel: Turn in the interest rate cycle
ereignisse.text: Rising long-term interest rates lower market values. Appraised values follow this development only with a delay, and it shows up in the unit price last.
The ifo business climate for residential construction stands at minus 22.7 points in August 2026, after minus 29.0 in the previous month. The value remains negative but is no longer falling.

bloecke.md:
A fund's annual and semi-annual reports are public. They contain the important key figures, including the occupancy rate, borrowing ratio, liquidity ratio, remaining terms of the leases, regional and sectoral breakdown and the amount of redemptions already announced. The last figure is the most important, because it shows how much money the fund has to pay out over the next twelve months.

Many figures on individual cases of write-downs and outflows are circulating for the period since 2023. In this lesson, only the earlier crisis is reliably documented, which is why it gives no percentage for the more recent one. Current figures should be taken from the annual report of the fund in question and not from a headline.

## REITs and property shares

A German **REIT** is a listed public limited company that pays neither corporation tax nor trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) at company level. In return, the REIT Act (REIT-Gesetz) of 2007 imposes several conditions. At least 90% of distributable profit must be distributed, at least 75% of income and assets must come from property, and at least 15% of the shares must be in free float, that is, held by shareholders with less than 3% each. No single shareholder may directly hold 10% or more. One exclusion has the greatest consequences, because existing rented residential properties built before 2007 may not be held in a German REIT. This was politically intended and has closed off most of the German property market to German REITs. The German REIT market has therefore remained a marginal phenomenon with a handful of companies to this day.

The large listed residential property groups are therefore ordinary public limited companies and not REITs. Vonovia and LEG are examples of this and not a recommendation. They pay tax on their profit at company level and decide freely on the dividend. Economically, REITs and property shares behave like other shares, with a daily stock exchange price, price fluctuations and a pronounced sensitivity to interest rates. This arises because the value of a property portfolio depends heavily on the discount rate. Two key figures are particularly important for the analysis: the gap between the stock market value and the net asset value, and the debt ratio (loan-to-value). For a company with 50% debt, every change in the value of the portfolio affects equity twice as strongly, for increases in value and losses in value alike.

It is often overlooked that property shares are already included in every broad world index. An additional REIT ETF is therefore a targeted overweighting of a small market segment and not a new asset class.

## Taxation

All three routes lead to income from capital assets. This is subject to 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus 5.5% solidarity surcharge, together 26.375% (Section 32d(1) EStG, Income Tax Act), plus church tax where applicable. Before that, the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 per person is deducted, or €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) EStG). The differences arise from the partial exemption and are large. The partial exemption is intended to compensate for taxes that a real estate fund already pays itself: on domestic rents, 15% corporation tax plus solidarity surcharge, together 15.825%. The illustrative calculation of net income leaves out these taxes at fund level.

bloecke.titel: Advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) on an accumulating real estate fund
bloecke.md:
Accumulating funds distribute nothing; a notional base return is taxed nevertheless (Section 18 InvStG). The base interest rate (Basiszins) as of 2 January 2026 is 3.20% (BMF circular of 13 January 2026). 70% of this is applied, that is, 2.24% of the value at the start of the year.

Unit value at the start of the year: €20,000

- Base return: €20,000 × 2.24% = €448
- Taxable after deducting 60% partial exemption: €179.20
- Tax: €179.20 × 26.375% = €47.26

Two limits can only reduce the amount. The base return is capped at the increase in value that the unit achieved during the year, and in a year with a falling unit price the advance lump sum does not apply at all. In periods of write-downs, it is therefore zero. The tax is due on the first working day of the following year; the bank debits it from the settlement account.

## Real estate crowdinvesting

Real estate crowdinvesting looks like co-ownership of a project, but legally it is a loan, almost always a **subordinated loan with a qualified subordination agreement** (qualifizierter Rangrücktritt). Because of the subordination, the investor is paid in insolvency only once all other creditors have been satisfied. In addition, the investor cannot demand repayment if it would drive the debtor into insolvency. The financing bank, by contrast, is secured by a first-ranking land charge (Grundschuld). Economically, the crowd investor therefore bears a risk like an equity investor but receives only a fixed, capped rate of interest like a lender.

The interest rates offered are well above what banks charge for mortgage financing secured by first-ranking charges. This premium compensates for the subordination and the associated default risk. It is neither a market failure nor a gift from the platform.

Regulation is less strict than for funds. Under the crowdfunding exemption of the Capital Investment Act (Section 2a VermAnlG), such offers are permitted without a prospectus; a brief investment information sheet (Vermögensanlagen-Informationsblatt) is sufficient. Private investors may, as a rule, subscribe at most €1,000 per issuer there. With a self-disclosure, up to €10,000 is possible if freely available assets amount to at least €100,000, or up to twice the monthly net income, but at most €25,000. Since 10 November 2021, the EU Crowdfunding Regulation has also applied. Platforms authorised under it have no fixed upper limit. Non-sophisticated investors there receive a risk warning before investing more than €1,000 or more than 5% of their net worth (whichever is higher), must explicitly consent and must demonstrate that they understand the investment and its risks. There is neither deposit protection nor a segregated pool of assets. If the project developer becomes insolvent, the money invested is lost.

With a share, the potential gain has no upper limit. With a loan, the best possible outcome is the agreed interest and the worst is a total loss. Ten successful projects at 6% interest a year, with capital spread evenly, together yield 60% of one project's stake per year of term. They therefore only make up for one total default once the term reaches 20 months.

There is relief on the tax side. The former offsetting limit of €20,000 a year for bad debt losses was abolished without replacement by the Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz) of 2 December 2024 and no longer applies in any open cases (Section 52(28) EStG). A final default can therefore be offset without limit against other capital income, but still only against such income and not against employment income (Section 20(6) sentence 1 EStG). Platforms are not banks and therefore do not usually withhold any tax. The interest must therefore be declared in the capital income annex.

## Limits of indirect investment

Three advantages of direct investment cannot be replicated with indirect investments. The first is leverage. No broker finances fund units on the terms of a mortgage, and a securities-backed loan is subject to margin calls when prices fall, whereas the bank does not repossess an occupied house because of interim price falls. The second is the ten-year period. The sale of a let property is tax-free after ten years (Section 23 EStG), the sale of fund units or shares never is. The third is depreciation. Annual depreciation of 2% to 3% of the building value as income-related expenses (Werbungskosten; Section 7(4) EStG) is only available for a property in your own name.

In return, everything that makes direct investment expensive and inflexible falls away: the incidental costs on entry, indivisibility, the concentration risk of a single location, management and dealing with tenants. With an investment amount of €20,000, the choice between a flat and a fund does not arise; only the indirect option is possible. Investors with €300,000 of own funds, by contrast, choose between two combinations. Direct investment offers leverage and a tax advantage and involves work; indirect investment offers diversification and liquidity without work.

Indirect property investments offer divisibility and diversification; in return, the investor gives up leverage and the tax privilege. Anyone who knows this trade-off can make a deliberate choice. An open-ended real estate fund is not a substitute for an instant-access savings account with a better return.

The unit price is based on appraisals instead of market prices, so the smooth path is a valuation artefact and not evidence of low risk.

A German REIT pays no corporation tax or trade tax at company level and in return must distribute 90%; because existing rented residential properties from before 2007 are excluded, the market has remained small.
The partial exemption largely determines net income; it is 60% or 80% for real estate funds and zero for dividends and loan interest.
Crowdinvesting is a subordinated loan without deposit protection whose return is limited, while the default risk extends to a total loss.

begriffe.text: Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen) made up of properties, with continuous issue of units. Since the KAGB of 2013, a minimum holding period of 24 months and a notice period of 12 months apply; in the event of liquidity shortages, redemptions may be suspended for up to 36 months.

Apparently low volatility of a unit price that arises only because it is based on periodic appraisals rather than market prices. The risk is no smaller as a result; it merely shows up later and abruptly.

Listed property company (AG) that is exempt from corporation tax and trade tax at company level and in return must distribute at least 90% of its distributable profit. In Germany, REITs have existed since the REITG of 2007; existing rented residential properties from before 2007 are excluded.

Flat-rate deduction from taxable fund income under Section 20 InvStG. It is 30% for equity funds, 15% for mixed funds, 60% for real estate funds and 80% for foreign real estate funds, and it applies to distributions, advance lump sums and capital gains.

Loan with a qualified subordination agreement (qualifizierter Rangrücktritt). Repayment can only be demanded once all other creditors have been paid, and only if it does not drive the debtor into insolvency. Common form of contract in real estate crowdinvesting, without segregated fund assets and without deposit protection.
